column1: # Ostler walk record -- written by scripts/post_walk_qa.sh
# Read by scripts/verify_walk_record.sh, which gates the customer download.
# The box is recorded as a hash: this repo is public.
# version_source says how the version was obtained. Anything other than
# measured(...) means the version is an assertion, not an observation.
# artefact_sha256 is the build this box was walked with. A version does
# NOT identify a build -- "1.0.50" named eleven distinct assemblies -- so
# this is the field the publish gate binds on. artefact_sha256_source
# reads measured(...) only when the DMG was found on the box and hashed
# there; that establishes WHICH BUILD, not that it was the one mounted.
# counts_scope says WHICH population pass/fail/cannot_run/broken describe.
# They are phase 1 ONLY -- parsed from run_box_walk.sh. Phase 2 (the cut
# manifest runtime proofs) contributes to verdict and qa_exit but emits no
# counts, so it is deliberately absent from these four numbers.
# below are the EXCEPTION: those DO cover both phases, because a phase-2-
# only failure still has to reach scripts/verify_walk_record.sh by name or
# its promote gate cannot scope its decision and refuses unscoped.
# READ verdict AND qa_exit FOR THE WHOLE-SUITE RESULT. The four counts are
# a subset and summing them will not reconcile against the console tally --
# 2026-08-24 that mismatch (13 here vs 33 on console) was carried for hours
# as an unexplained discrepancy in a v1.0.44 verdict that was correct all
# along, because these keys were unqualified.

column2: measured(shasum -a 256 of OstlerInstaller-1.0.131.dmg on the walked box, the DMG the walk staged per its walk-dmg marker; re-hash equals the staged sha)
full: everything; required before any console walk and any public tag

column1: # instrument_rev answers the question this record has never
# answered: WHICH PROBES graded that artefact. The subject is
# named six ways above -- version, version_source,
# and the instrument was named nowhere.
# It matters because the probes do NOT come from the artefact. In
# --from-dmg mode ttywalk.sh copies the .app Resources verbatim,
# and gui/project.yml bundles box_walk_probes ZERO times, so the
# suite that runs is the one in THIS checkout. A walk is therefore
# artefact X judged by instrument Y, and only X was recorded.
# The case that forced it: no_person_holds_two_contact_cards
# gained a collision-opportunity measure in #1549. Before it, a
# clean graph printed a bare pass; after it, the same graph prints
# EARNED or UNEXERCISED. BOTH WRITE THE SAME `pass` HERE. Reading
# this file later, nobody could tell an earned zero from a vacuous
# one -- which is the exact distinction that probe exists to make.
# instrument_source says HOW the value was obtained, same idiom as
# version_source. A sha that does not describe the probes that ran
# is worse than no sha, so local edits under box_walk_probes are
# named rather than hidden behind a clean-looking commit id.
# 🔴 A CLEAN SHA DOES NOT MEAN main. It means the probes are EXACTLY
# that commit, which may be a branch, a tag or a detached head. The
# v1.0.71 walk ran from a harness branch that was main plus five
# reset fixes: a correct, clean, committed sha that was nonetheless
# not main. Resolve the sha before assuming the lineage -- this
# field answers WHICH probes ran, never WHERE they came from.
# stores_provenance answers the question every store-reading probe
# begs and none of them state: was the graph this walk measured
# CREATED by this artefact, or CARRIED OVER from a previous install?
# or people_count_agreement means something different in each case. A
# reset does NOT wipe: ttywalk.sh runs the shipped uninstaller if it can
# find one and says so when it cannot.
# cold answers whether the box held NO Ostler state before the install:
# PROVEN(...) carries the per-root file counts before and after the wipe;
# NOT_COLD(...) means carried-over state may sit under every count in this
# record. verify_walk_record.sh refuses verdict CLEAN without cold PROVEN.

column2: PROVEN(files outside the allowlist, before->after per root: .ostler:132594->0 Ostler:0->0 Ostler:87991->0 Ostler:25->0 )

column1: # grounding_seed answers the one question assistant_answers_grounded
# begs and has never stated: was this box SEEDED before the probe
# asked? An unseeded box and a broken product produce the SAME red.
# That probe is red on 17 of the 21 committed records, and not one
# of them says which kind of red it was. Five states: seeded,
# skipped, absent, failed, unrun -- plus not-recorded when the
# marker could not be read, which is NOT the same as unrun.

column2: not-recorded(no ~/.walk-grounding-seed-run on the box; this walk predates the marker or the read failed)
